subject: src/ast/real-elixir-analyzer.ts
mechanism: SOURCE-level injection into the analyzer file, then the real script/m14/run-fixtures.ts against the edited analyzer; the subject is restored in a finally and verified by hash
whyNotTheSharedHarness: script/m14/mutate-analyzer.ts wraps analyzer OUTPUT and lives in script/m14/**, which the workstream ownership table gives to the supervisor. These mutants edit the SOURCE. Registering them in the shared list is reported as a need, not made here.
claimLevel: L4-scope: the mutants below are the ones this lane added; the lane's PRE-EXISTING mutant set (87 mutants, script/m14/mutate-analyzer.ts ids prefixed elixir/) was NOT re-run here and is out of this file's scope.

log.description: The `uses` emission for a member field read is deleted — the field read goes silent again, which is the pre-ELIXIR_FIX2 state. Caught by member-read-uses.
The member field read is relabelled `calls` instead of `uses` — the edge exists but carries the wrong type, which is the Q4 failure the ontology asks about. Caught by member-read-uses.

The receiver's first character is no longer checked, so a CAPITALIZED remote callee is double-labelled `uses` on top of its `calls` edge — every remote call published twice under two labels. Caught by member-read-uses.
log.detail: pass 63 / fail 2; failing fixtures: member-read-uses, remote-ref-forms

log.description: The `->` pattern-position guard is removed, so binding a field in a clause head publishes a `uses` edge — a pattern is not an evaluation (ER-D7). Caught by member-read-uses.
The `exports` pass is deleted — the module's published surface disappears from the graph. Caught by export-surface.
log.detail: pass 63 / fail 2; failing fixtures: export-surface, unnamed-module-owner

log.description: The visibility test is dropped, so defp/defmacrop/defguardp/@typep are published as exports — on this corpus 7,959 names no importer can bind, and no oracle can catch it because both sides would be written from the same wrong rule. Caught by export-surface.
Struct fields (Property) join the exported kinds, so each field is published as an importable unit — membership already rides `contains`, per the exports-family ruling. Caught by export-surface.
log.detail: pass 63 / fail 2; failing fixtures: export-surface, unnamed-module-owner

log.description: The `owner === name` guard is dropped, so a defstruct's own symbol publishes `exports M -> M` — the same self-loop the contains pass suppresses (EX-L3). Caught by export-surface.
The `overrides` pass is deleted — the language's override construct is read but not published, which is the pre-ELIXIR_FIX2 state. Caught by use-defoverridable.

The overridable-SET lookup is dropped, so EVERY definition in a `use N` module is published as overriding N — the fabrication the whole ruling turns on, since most definitions in a `use N` module are new functions. Caught by use-defoverridable.

The `defoverridable SomeModule` arm stops requiring that SomeModule be DECLARED in this file, so the arm names a function of a module whose function list was never read — the exact fabrication the arm's comment warns about, and the shape that would make `use GenServer` + `def child_spec` fire for every `use` target. Caught by use-defoverridable.

The LIVE quote gate is defeated: `defoverridable` is recorded even when the walk is inside quoted code, so a `defoverridable` inside a `__using__` TEMPLATE could be credited to the module that only DEFINES the template. NOT CAUGHT, and the survival is adjudicated EQUIVALENT with a measurement rather than waved through — see `equivalence` below. The first version of this mutant deleted a SECOND, redundant guard inside recordOverridable and also survived, byte-identical, because the walk already routes every quoted call away from the branch chain; a guard that cannot fire is dead code wearing a safety net's name, so the redundant one was deleted and the mutant now attacks the gate that is live.

declaredEquivalent.claim: Removing the walk's quote gate for `defoverridable` cannot change any output on this corpus, so no fixture can catch it and its survival is not a hole in the suite.
declaredEquivalent.measurement: Probe F3 in validation/m14/elixir/elixir-construct-census.ts counts `defoverridable` sites that are BOTH inside a quote AND credited to a module scope — the only shape the gate can change, because a mark inside a quoted `__using__` body is credited to the MACRO's function scope, and a function scope is never the target of a `use`. Measured over 601 derived .ex/.exs files: E1 26 sites / 14 files, of which F1 (no enclosing def body) 10 / 3, F2 (credited to a module) 10 / 3, and **F3 (inside a quote AND credited to a module) 0 / 0**. The counts decompose exactly: 26 = 16 enclosed in a def body + 10 module-credited, and none of the 10 is quoted. Corroborated by applying the mutant and diffing the analyzer's own output on the fixture: identical relationships, symbols and metadata.

log.description: The §4 default is removed from pushRel, so an edge whose SITE carries no code loses its machine-readable reason code — measured before the fix at 49,007/49,007 calls, 930/930 references, 1,187/1,187 instantiates and 73/73 implements. Caught by struct-update, whose instantiates row pins meta.reasonCode and meta.reasonCodeSource (the marker that the edge RELIES on the default rather than a site code — which is what keeps the guarantee a live branch instead of dead code).

The EX-A15 regression this branch inherited: the unconditional binary_operator read is restored, so `defmacro (..)` publishes a macro named "(" with arity 3. Caught by paren-operator-forms, which has been failing on the inherited baseline.

The P6 fix is reverted: an un-nameable `defmodule` pushes no scope, so the ENCLOSING module keeps ownership and contains/exports name the members of a module the corpus never names. This is the pre-fix state and it published `contains ExceptionTest -> foo`. Caught by unnamed-module-owner, whose forbids name exactly those edges.

The unnamed scope is pushed but never popped, so every later declaration in the FILE loses its owner. The fixture's POSITIVE CONTROL (`defmodule Named` and its members) is the edge set that disappears, which is why the fixture pins the named case as well as forbidding the unnamed one.

The struct half of P6 is reverted: a `defstruct` inside an un-nameable module is named after the ENCLOSING module, forging a struct that module does not define. Caught by unnamed-module-owner's forbidSymbols on the two fields.
